hardness_axes.name: Discover
hardness_axes.reasoning: The instruction states only symptoms (resumed cells retrieve differently, wrong generation pinned, out-of-band values). The solver must discover from the tree/runtime: (1) the ledger JSONL under data/ledger carries sealed-vs-working markers that define the committed generation, (2) resumed checkpoint blobs carry per-block scale frames the unpacker silently drops, (3) the sheet keyed by the committed generation lives beside a bait sheet the resolver currently reads, (4) ops/prefer.toml gates a build-time rematerialization that undoes naive source edits, (5) mixed cells must exclude withdrawn segments per ledger marks. None of these appear in instruction.md.

hardness_axes.name: Synthesize
hardness_axes.reasoning: The answer spans two Rust crates (core: blob unpack + mixed-cell assembly; rank: generation binding + scale resolution), a build-authority config (ops/prefer.toml), the ledger data format, and the committed sheet family. No single file contains the solution; the solver must model how binding -> sheet row -> scale -> similarity fusion -> metrics propagate into every report cell.

hardness_axes.name: Diagnose
hardness_axes.reasoning: Symptoms-only instruction: 'resumed runs no longer retrieve like their cold twins', 'rows pin the wrong generation', 'values sit outside the published bands'. Causes (dropped block-scale frames, newest-line binding instead of sealed-line binding, bait sheet, withdrawn-segment inclusion, build-time source rematerialization) must be inferred from behavior and code reading.

hardness_axes.name: Navigate coupling
hardness_axes.reasoning: Fixes couple: correcting the two rank sources without flipping ops/prefer.toml is undone on the verifier's rebuild (the build script rematerializes them from seed templates while the binding stays on the working line). The scale value depends on the generation binding, so fixing the sheet choice alone still reads the wrong row. Mixed cells depend on both the unpack fix and the withdrawn-segment roster, so greening cold cells alone leaves mix cells out of band.

hardness_axes.name: Reason beyond training
hardness_axes.reasoning: The scale value enters a score fusion (cosine plus scale-weighted prior) and a soft-assignment agreement statistic, so its effect on retrieval and clustering metrics is not the textbook monotone-softmax case; block-scale checkpoint framing and sealed-vs-working ledger semantics are bespoke to this tree. There is no in-distribution recipe (HMAC/schema-validation/Monte-Carlo class) that pattern-matches to the solution.

discovery_budget.discovery: The ledger JSONL distinguishes sealed (committed) lines from working lines; every report cell must bind to the newest sealed index, while the resolver currently binds to the newest line of any state.
discovery_budget.planned_location: data/ledger/journal.jsonl marks plus rank/src/knot.rs behavior; semantics documented only as outcome language in docs.
discovery_budget.why_instruction_must_not_reveal: Naming the sealed-marker rule would turn the generation fix into a one-line transcription; the instruction only says the committed generation must be reported, using the durable-vs-live outcome vocabulary.

discovery_budget.discovery: Resumed checkpoint blobs carry per-block scale frames; the unpacker drops them and returns raw mantissas, which silently changes vector norms and breaks cold/resume retrieval parity.
discovery_budget.planned_location: Binary framing of data/checkpoints/resume_*.ckpt plus core/src/lens.rs.
discovery_budget.why_instruction_must_not_reveal: Stating that resumed blobs are block-scaled is the diagnosis; the instruction only states the parity symptom (resumed cells no longer retrieve like their cold twins).

discovery_budget.discovery: ops/prefer.toml holds a binding mode; while it stays on the working line, the rank crate's build script rematerializes the two rank sources from seed templates on every build, so naive source-only fixes are undone when the verifier rebuilds.
discovery_budget.why_instruction_must_not_reveal: This is the authority-coupling discovery; revealing it reduces the task to a config flip plus edits. The instruction only requires that the report come from rebuilding the sources.

discovery_budget.discovery: Mixed cells must be assembled from the ledger's composition roster, excluding withdrawn segments; the assembler currently concatenates every segment present on disk.
discovery_budget.planned_location: core/src/weave.rs plus withdrawal marks in data/ledger/journal.jsonl.
discovery_budget.why_instruction_must_not_reveal: Naming the withdrawal rule turns mixed-cell repair into transcription; the instruction only says mixed cells disagree with the documentation.

discovery_budget.discovery: The scale sheet family is keyed by generation and only one family is committed; the resolver currently reads the bait sheet that tracks the working line, which yields out-of-band scale values and mis-fused scores.
discovery_budget.why_instruction_must_not_reveal: Pointing at the correct sheet file is the answer; the instruction only requires the value to sit inside the published band.

attack_path.summary: Run entrypoint -> observe red cells -> diff cold/resume blob framing -> read ledger marks -> fix unpack + binding + sheet + roster -> discover rebuild rematerialization -> flip binding authority -> converge all six cells and determinism.
attack_path.reasoning: The expected solver path: run the entrypoint and see out-of-band cells; compare cold and resumed blob bytes to find block-scale frames and fix the unpacker; read the ledger to find sealed markers and fix the binding; follow the binding into the sheet lookup and fix the sheet family; fix the mixed-cell roster; then find that a fresh rebuild reverts the two rank fixes, trace the build script to ops/prefer.toml, and flip the binding mode. Only after all five coordinate do the parity, band, generation, mixed-cell, rebuild-equality, and byte-identity tests all pass.

smallest_plausible_patch.summary: Approximately 60-90 lines of semantic change across five files: block-scale application in the unpacker, sealed-line selection in the binder, committed-sheet lookup in the resolver, roster filtering in the assembler, one config key flip.
smallest_plausible_patch.reasoning: Each site is a genuine semantic rewrite, not a polarity flip: the unpacker must parse and apply per-block frames; the binder must parse and filter ledger states; the resolver must key the committed family by the bound generation; the assembler must honor withdrawal marks; the config flip only helps once both rank sources are also correct. Hand-writing the report instead fails the rebuild-equality, trace-reconstruction, and byte-identity tests.

collapse_audit.reasoning: Audited against the known collapse patterns: no knob checklist in docs (bands are outcome tables, not fix maps); no answer values in fixtures (the surface fixture is explicitly untrustworthy bait); fix-path names are opaque and decoys rhyme with them, so grep and shape scanning mislead; the smallest passing patch spans five locations in three roots with max test share 0.44; the build-authority gate undoes the most likely partial solve (source-only edits) on the verifier rebuild, which blocks one-pass completion; scale enters score fusion and soft-assignment agreement, so temperature is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
collapse_audit.residual_hardness: Even with the file tree visible, the solver must (a) reverse the block-scale frame layout from binary fixtures, (b) infer sealed-vs-working ledger semantics from data plus outcome docs, (c) realize the sheet family is generation-keyed and which family is committed, (d) discover the rematerialization by observing its own edits being reverted, and (e) keep all six cells plus determinism green simultaneously. These survive full disclosure of the layout.
